The build process uses `cargo build --release --locked`, which ensures reproducible builds by respecting Cargo.lock, a best practice in Rust packaging. There are no signs of malicious behavior such as network exfiltration, use of `eval`, obfuscated code, or unexpected downloads. The dependencies and build tools (rustup, cmake) are appropriate for a Rust-based application with potential C/C++ components or build-time requirements. The `options=("!lto")` disables LTO, which is a common workaround for build issues in some Rust packages and not inherently suspicious.

The package adheres to typical AUR packaging standards and shows no evidence of supply chain compromise.
</details>
